title: Rectifiers and power supplies
idea: Diodes turn AC into DC pulses; capacitors and inductors smooth them; a bleeder drains the capacitors when the power is off. Switchmode supplies work at high frequency, so their parts are small.

rows: Pulses at twice the AC frequency
Pulses at twice the AC frequency

compare.how: Two diodes and a center-tapped transformer.
60 Hz transformer and filter: big and heavy.

traps.wrong: It acts as a fuse for excess voltage
traps.why: A bleeder drains the filter capacitors; it doesn't protect anything.
Diodes rectify. The filter is capacitors and inductors.
A bridge uses four diodes and no center tap.

traps.wrong: The ripple frequency is twice that of a full-wave rectifier
traps.why: Backwards: full-wave ripple is twice half-wave's.
360 degrees is full-wave. Half-wave keeps only one half.

traps.wrong: A series of DC pulses at the same frequency as the AC input
traps.why: That's half-wave. Full-wave gives two pulses per cycle.
Switchmode supplies have more parts, but smaller ones.
